chapter: Armstrong, Big Sid and Joe Glaser
title: Joe Glaser as Armstrong's manager and how he bought his contract
summary: Glaser did not pay Louis's bills; he bought Louis's contract for $500 from a man who had beaten him, took abuse from Southerners for working with Black musicians, and Louis called him his father.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Was possibly the reason that he never worried about money the fact that Joe Glaser always seemed to take care of everything and he didn't have to worry?
Oh, he didn't have to worry about anything. He was working on a salary, like, and Joe Glaser would put the rest away for him, you know.
But Joe Glaser paid all the bills, didn't he? I mean, whenever -- Louie could run up a bill and if they sent it to Joe Glaser, it would be paid?
Louie had to pay it himself --
-- out of his money. No, he was -- that was independent. You know, if Glaser did that, you know how much Glaser -- well, he made Glaser the millionaire 'cause

Glaser's mother didn't want to be bothered with him anymore because he was so bad, Glaser was, he made a little gal pregnant, and when the mother found that out, then she disowned him. She didn't want to be bothered with him.
But wasn't Glaser associated with the Chicago gangsters?
Yeah, at one time. He wasn't associated, he was, like, a stoolie.
Did he meet Louie in Chicago?

He bought Louie from a guy that beat Louie on the boat that had Louie under contract. And coming back he didn't want to be bothered with Louie again -- they had an argument or something and they had a fight. So when they came back to the states, see, he sold Louie to Joe Glaser for $500, I think it was.

And Glaser was a go-getter. He went on the road with -- he was the manager then with Louie playing these southern gigs. And Louie used to tell him how they was all so scared because them crackers was giving Joe hell because he was a Jew and working with the Negroes, and that did it, you know.

Yeah, and, well, Joe took all that abuse from the crackers down there. But he's quite a salesman, too, you know. And if you don't know Glaser, you would swear he was about the worst gangster in the world, and the guy, he's got a big heart, too, a real nice guy. But you have to know him.

And you should hear he and Louie arguing together. Louie said that's his father. He said that Joe Glasser was his father, "we understand each other." I wished they did understand each other. They'd cuss each other out, I'd swear I couldn't understand that part.
